Title: Tipper overturns after being hit by lorry at Sungai Buloh junction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lorry crashed into another lorry at a traffic light junction in Sungai Buloh in an incident captured in a video.
Sungai Buloh police chief superintendent Mohd Hafiz Muhammad Nor said the incident occurred about 5pm last Friday when a lorry was returning to its depot in Batu Arang.
"The lorry collided with another lorry while approaching a traffic light junction against a red light," he said in a statement.
The collision caused the tipper to overturn, leaving its driver injured.
Hafiz said police received a report on the accident at about 6.55pm on the same day.
"Both lorry drivers went to the Sungai Buloh police headquarters to lodge accident reports. The case is being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Road users are advised to remain cautious, obey traffic rules and prioritise safety," he said.
Those with information can contact traffic investigating officer Inspector Mohd Nizam Othman at 017-625 4779 or the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters operations room at 03-6156 1222.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Resurfacing of Taman Sri Sentosa main road scheduled to start in early 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Resurfacing works on the main road of Taman Sri Sentosa are scheduled to begin early next year, while pothole repairs in the residential areas there will commence in the near future.
Lembah Pantai member of parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has approved the allocation for the resurfacing of the main road.
Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said funds have also been secured to repair roads in residential areas overseen by management bodies that are unable to bear the repair costs.
"Early next year, Housing and Local Government Ministry will also begin works to replace the lifts in every block at AC4," he said when speaking at the Lembah Pantai Deepavali celebration in Taman Sri Sentosa tonight.
However, Fahmi said an application to convert the land in front of AC4 into a free parking area for residents is still awaiting approval.
He also expressed his intention to hold a free breakfast programme once a month in Taman Sri Sentosa, with the first session scheduled to start at 8am on Nov 28.
Regarding school preparations, Fahmi said back-to-school vouchers will be distributed in the Lembah Pantai parliamentary constituency over the next few weeks to help families prepare their children's necessities.
He said the Early Schooling Assistance of RM200 per student will begin to be channeled early next year.
Fahmi said parents must be present at the school to receive the aid, simultaneously giving them the opportunity to meet with their respective children's teachers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drug-positive lorry driver arrested for transporting Bangladeshis with expired passes
Article:
KOTA BARU: A drug-positive lorry driver was arrested in Batu Melintang, Jeli, yesterday for allegedly transporting three Bangladeshi men who had overstayed their visit passes from Terengganu to Perak.
The suspect, in his 40s, was driving a green Fuso lorry when he was detained during a snap check at the 6th Mile Roadblock in Batu Melintang at 11.30pm.
Jeli deputy police chief deputy superintendent said all three Bangladeshis held expired visit passes.
"The lorry driver also tested positive for drugs, and police seized a bottle of liquid suspected to be ketum water found inside the lorry.
"The Bangladeshis had been living in Malaysia for more than three years and working in various sectors.
"All of them have been detained to assist in investigations, while a remand application for the driver will be made at the Jeli magistrate's court for four days," he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 55E and Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, as well as Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Preserving the Peranakan way of life
Article:
ONE of the most distinctive and colourful aspects of Malaysian multiculturalism is that syncretic amalgam of the Chinese, more specifically Hokkien, way of life infused with Malay cultural elements that is the Peranakan heritage of the Babas and Nyonyas.
The adoption of the sarong in the Nyonya way of dressing and Malay cooking style and ingredients — complete with Nyonya ceramic table wares — have made Peranakan architecture and restaurants a mainstay of tourist attractions, particularly in the former Straits settlements of Penang and Melaka.
Alas, like many things that have become an integral part of Malaysian heritage and folklore, the Peranakan way of life has become quaint and dated. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has just sounded the alarm about its threat of extinction. Speaking at the opening of the 37th International Baba Nyonya Convention in George Town on Saturday, Nov 21, he revealed that there were now only about 1,000 active practitioners of this way of life in the state.
"A language can fade in one generation if parents stop using it at home. A beading technique can vanish when the last person who knows it puts down her needle," Chow had said. If this is the reality, one must wonder if anything can be done this late in the day to try to reverse the decline and ultimate death of the Peranakan way as a living facet of the overall Malaysian social and cultural fabric.
If such a distinct and unique culture way of life is fast dying, can anything really be done to preserve it? Apparently, the Penang government is doing its bit. Chow spoke of gazetting Penang Dondang Sayang and the Penang Hokkien dialect as official State Heritage on Oct 10. A total of RM25 million has also been channelled through the George Town World Heritage Incorporated since 2024 to conserve historical buildings and assets, including Peranakan townhouses and temples.
However, there is only so much official intervention can do to arrest a culture on its death throes unless the community itself does its bit to keep it alive. The spirit is obviously willing, as the convention which brought together delegates from Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Australia attests.
The delegates must themselves come up with concrete proposals to popularise Peranakan language and other cultural elements among the community's younger generation from the Baba and Nyonya community. The fate of such a unique way of life ultimately rests with the community itself and the steps it must commit to take to perpetuate it within each Baba and Nyonya family unit.
It will be a sad day indeed if only the physical aspects of the Peranakan culture live on one day in museums and heritage buildings as mere tourist attractions instead of it living and breathing as part of the Malaysian cultural mosaic. It will be a most tragic irony if the Peranakan culture continues to thrive as cultural relics instead of remaining as a lived-in tradition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak polls: DAP names 9 candidates, more to be announced
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak DAP has announced another seven candidates for the 13th Sarawak state election.
Its chairman Chong Chieng Jen will defend his Padungan seat, while Violet Yong will defend her Pending seat.
The other candidates are retired policeman Lim Nee Kon for Opar, Michael Kong (Kota Sentosa), Jordan Soo (Batu Kitang), Sim Kiat Leng (Batu Kawa) and Bandar Kuching Member of Parliament Dr Kelvin Yii for Batu Lintang.
Speaking at the party's mobilisation night here tonight, Chong said the line-up reflected DAP's intention to strengthen its presence in the Sarawak State legislative assembly and provide effective opposition representation.
"One thing we can be certain of is that after the upcoming state election, Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will still form the state government…the importance of having a functioning opposition to serve as a check and balance should not be overlooked," he said.
On Friday, DAP Sarawak announced two candidates for the coming polls, naming Irene Wong for Pelawan and Stanley Chiew (Bukit Assek), both in Sibu.
The party is expected to announce its decisions on the seats in Sarikei, Bintulu and Miri soon.
In the 12th Sarawak state election held on Dec 18, 2021, GPS secured 76 of the 82 seats contested, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats and DAP secured two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1-year-old boy reported missing in Kuala Krai
Article:
KOTA BARU: A 20-month-old boy has been reported missing from the grounds of his family home in Kampung Bechah Salak, Kuala Krai since 4pm.
Kuala Krai Fire and Rescue station chief Nik Ahmad Afsham Nik Pa said they received a distress call about the boy via the NG999 system at 6.37pm and a team arrived at the scene seven minutes later.
He said the family searched the house for the boy and lodged a police report after failing to find him.
"A search and rescue operation was conducted around the home, including at a 1m-deep fish pond located 50m away.
"The boy's family had pumped the water out of the pond with the help of villagers and firefighters, but the boy was not found," he said when contacted today.
The search was expanded to the nearby forest area. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Beijing's snub could give Japan's PM Takaichi a lift at home
Article:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi got a cold reception in her first outing to China, but Beijing's "blatant" snub —  including a visibly scaled-down welcome — could galvanise her conservative base, experts said.
Her trip to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit marked the first time she met Chinese President Xi Jinping face-to-face since her comments about Taiwan last year plunged relations between the two major Asian powers to historic lows.
Takaichi suggested that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event that China attacked Taiwan, and a furious China, which views the democratic island as part of its territory, retaliated with trade restrictions and warned its citizens not to travel to Japan.
That backdrop meant "there was little she could expect" from the trip, and "little was indeed achieved in terms of Japan-China relations", Noriyuki Kawamura, a professor emeritus at Nagoya University of Foreign Studies, said.
Takaichi, as expected, failed to secure a formal sit-down with Xi on the Apec sidelines.
She was greeted by relatively low-ranking officials on arrival in Shenzhen and without the elaborate performances that welcomed other world leaders, prompting headlines at home about China's "blatant" snub.
Takaichi was also seen struggling to step off her plane because of what appeared to be an unusually large gap between the plane's door and the top of the boarding stairs.
That prompted online speculation it had been done intentionally by Beijing to embarrass her.
Japan's top government spokesman Minoru Kihara told reporters on Friday that they had been aware of the gap.
"Since we had received that information in advance at the site, we took appropriate measures to ensure safety," Kihara said, without specifying whether the Japanese or Chinese side had provided the information.
"As a result, Prime Minister Takaichi disembarked from the aircraft safely," he said.
A mostly expressionless Xi twice exchanged handshakes with Takaichi during the two-day forum —  first very briefly and then for about 10 seconds as he listened to her speak with a beaming smile on her face.
However, experts say the cold shoulder might not be all bad news for her domestically, potentially stoking support from the most hardcore of pro-Takaichi voters.
"The way they see it, she didn't give in to the snub she got, but shook hands with (Xi) as many as two times with dignity," Kawamura said.
Yu Uchiyama, a political science professor at the University of Tokyo, also said that China's chilly reception was unlikely to cost her popularity at home, pointing out that public support for her didn't wane even after her Taiwan statement a year ago.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see her loyal supporters become upset by the way she was mocked and grow more resentful toward China," Uchiyama said.
A day after the summit ended, China again said Japan's "most urgent task is to correct its wrong words and actions on the Taiwan issue as soon as possible", according to a foreign ministry spokesman.
Takaichi's critics at home, however, saw the Apec summit as proof of Japan's diminished global standing under her stewardship and her lack of diplomatic acumen.
Footage circulated widely online of Takaichi approaching President Donald Trump after a group photo and patting him on the back, only to be ignored by the US leader who instead walked away with Xi.
That viral image, coupled with Trump's historic trilateral summit with Xi and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, fed social media narratives that she is not taken seriously on the global stage.
"Since when did Japan become such a shameful country? The whole world is laughing at us," one post on X said.
Still, concerns for Japan's global reputation could easily be swept aside by a recent surge in distrust towards foreigners that will ultimately help sustain Takaichi's popularity, Uchiyama said.
Complaints about overtourism and soaring land prices linked to foreign investment have sparked Takaichi's push for tighter control of visa rules, prompting voters sceptical on immigration to coalesce around her policies.
On the back of this simmering sentiment "resembling xenophobia", Uchiyama said, it is possible that "people will start to think, 'why is Takaichi treated so badly overseas when she works so hard in her own country?'"
The writer is from AFP

Title: COP31 climate talks collapse as EU and others reject deal
Article:
ANTALYA: UN climate talks collapsed on Sunday as the European Union and others rejected a final draft deal put forward by COP31 presidents Turkiye and Australia, saying it was too weak to advance the fight against global warming.
The failed talks reflect world governments' struggle this year to muster ambitious action to address the worsening consequences of climate change, as wars, economic pressures and other crises compete for their attention.
After more than two weeks of negotiations that spilled two days into overtime — making it the longest COP on record — Turkiye's conference president Murat Kurum said at the closing plenary that he could see there was no agreement and confirmed he would not advance any new text.
"There is nothing to do, we did all that we could," he said. "There will be no new text from now on."
He later left the stage in the midst of speeches being delivered by country representatives.
Australia's COP31 president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, called the outcome "very disappointing" and said disagreements over fuels and climate finance were the dealbreakers.
The last time UN climate talks failed to get a deal adopted by all was in Copenhagen in 2009.
Ireland's Environment Minister Darragh O'Brien said the European Union could not support the proposed deal in part because it made no mention of the fossil fuels that scientists say drive global warming.
"It is unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuel, no reference to transitioning away from fossil fuels," he said.
Saudi Arabia and other big oil producer countries had lobbied hard to keep their mention out of the text, according to observers at the summit.
Panama also said it could not support the text because it failed to address the scale and urgency of the climate crisis.
This year's COP is the first since the UN's environmental body in October confirmed the rise in global temperature was set to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit), a threshold countries agreed at Paris climate talks over a decade ago to try not to exceed, and beyond which extreme weather impacts intensify.
Belgium's Climate Minister Jean-Luc Crucke said the failure of the deal was a difficult outcome, but appropriate.
"It's not the end of multilateralism, but there has to be courage to say no," he said.
While a blow to efforts to ratchet up international action, the failure to agree a political declaration in Antalya does not erase the obligations agreed by previous UN conferences or remove the technical and legal frameworks governing multilateral action against climate change.
PRESSURE FROM SAUDI ARABIA AND OTHER OIL PRODUCERS
The failed deal had acknowledged the planet's projected temperature overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies to eventually reverse it.
That was a big ask from oil-producing countries.
While scientists say removing carbon from the atmosphere — when paired with steep emissions cuts — is vital to avoiding the worst impacts of climate change, critics of the proposed deal said they worried the carbon removal language would be used as a licence to keep pumping oil.
A representative for the Saudi delegation, which supported the deal's mention of carbon removal, told the summit at the closing plenary that he was surprised at the resistance to technology, which he said offered a concrete solution.
Developing countries had also criticised the deal for not providing sufficient new climate finance to help them adapt to a warming planet. The deal had called for a tripling of such finance, but did not specify from what baseline.
The failed deal had also included a goal put forward by Turkiye to expand electricity's share of total final world energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035, from around 23 per cent now.
Proponents of that pledge said it could cut greenhouse gas emissions by speeding the transition away from fuel-powered cars, furnaces, and other equipment. But critics said it could force more costs onto poor nations without providing a clear path away from fossil fuels.
The COP process is the main vehicle through which countries coordinate their efforts to curb global warming. Its annual meeting provides an opportunity for nations to signal they are willing to work together to find solutions and help finance the problems rising temperatures cause.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AI-driven growth lifts dollar, but direction remains uncertain
Article:
ARTIFICIAL intelligence is increasingly shaping the fortunes of the US dollar, or at least the investment race surrounding it. The only problem is currency experts cannot agree whether that's for better or worse.
Estimates vary, but many analysts say AI is directly or indirectly responsible for at least a third of US gross domestic product expansion this year.
That alone seems straightforward, but the extent to which the dollar's value is AI-linked is more nuanced.
At its most basic, the lift to US growth, inflation and interest rate expectations from the AI boom is clearly dollar positive — as long as the United States retains its edge and the lion's share of the investment being ploughed into it.
While that may change as
the early US investment surge slows, we're not there yet in most people's eyes.
The dollar is clearly reflecting expectations that the Federal Reserve may hike rates aggressively to cool an AI-fuelled boom and rein in inflation, with investors convinced the economy can take it while other central banks hesitate.
Since the Iran war began at the end of February, the US economy has brushed aside the related
fuel-price shock with ease, and the AI story seems largely responsible.
US economic surprise indexes compiled by Citi have hit their most positive level in three years this month, contrasting starkly with euro zone equivalents, which have turned negative again for the first time in four months.
Little surprise, then, that euro/dollar has fallen below US$1.10 this week for the first time since March last year, while the broader dollar index has hit its best level in more than 19 months.
But wait. This dollar surge is happening just as Big Tech investors get the jitters over AI valuations and on fear of a capital expenditure slowdown after Democratic victories in the midterm elections prompt calls for at least some data-centre pushback.
The scale of the shakeout in AI-linked stocks has been withering for six weeks, seeing almost 30 per cent wiped off the US Philadelphia Semiconductor Index since early October.
So, why hasn't the fabled "AI dollar" gone with it?
Is the greenback simply lagging, or staying laser-focused on pumped-up Fed rate-rise expectations? Or maybe it's getting a safety bid from worries about equity-market turbulence?
Barclays FX strategists this week reckoned their bullish "AI dollar" view remains very much intact for next year.
Their take hinges on the fact the dollar is mainly tracking AI capex numbers that have been driving GDP outperformance, forcing the Fed to rethink the level of slack left in the economy and where neutral interest rates lie.
But there are as many questions in that as there are answers.
Bank of America's November survey of global fund managers offers some insight.
The poll showed asset managers this month cut tech allocations by the most in 20 years, with a record net near 40 per cent of respondents saying companies are "over-investing".
Perhaps most telling, more than half of the funds expect at least one hyperscaler to cut capex in the next six months.
So AI capex can still be your lodestar, but it may not mean the "AI dollar" is the slam dunk for 2027 that markets have recently rushed to price.
However, there's another way to view the nexus between AI and the dollar.
Deutsche Bank introduces its idea of "chipdollars", akin to the petrodollars of old.
World chip trade now exceeds oil and gas for the first time in history, it says, suggesting a less favourable outlook for the dollar.
The gist of Deutsche's view is that most US-designed chips are made outside the US, mainly in Asia.
As chip demand has soared and prices have risen, huge surpluses have built up in these countries. Much of that cash has been recycled into US capital markets, mostly equities rather than Treasury debt as in the past.
However, a big problem is that equities are three times more volatile than Treasuries, and tech stocks up to 10 times more so.
"Growing dollar dependence on inherently riskier capital should spill into higher US dollar volatility over time," Deutsche strategist Mallika Sachdeva wrote.
There's no doubt the "AI dollar" is now a thing. It's just that it could go either way next year — not unlike its analog predecessor.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: High tide phenomenon raises flood risk in Sabak, Pengkalan Chepa
Article:
KOTA BARU: The high tide phenomenon expected to occur tonight has increased the risk of flooding around Sabak and Pengkalan Chepa, after several areas there were inundated by up to 0.5m this afternoon.
Pengkalan Chepa Fire and Rescue station chief Mohd Faizol Hisham Abdullah said his team was on standby for a possible rise in water levels, particularly if the high tide phenomenon occurred as forecast.
He said monitoring carried out about 2pm today found that seven villages and several areas around Sabak had been inundated due to the area's tendency to experience waterlogging, as well as the lack of an adequate drainage system.
The affected areas are Kampung Pantai Sabak, Kampung Tebing Tinggi, Kampung Pulau Gajah, Kampung Kemumin, the area around SK Sabak, Masjid Lama Kampung Sabak, Pantai Nusuk, Kampung Sering, Kampung Gajah Mati and Kampung Pulau Belanga.
"Water levels in several locations have reached about 0.5m. Fire and rescue personnel are on standby for a possible rise in water levels, particularly if the high tide phenomenon occurs tonight.
"The temporary relief centre at SK Sabak has also been identified as a shelter for victims should evacuation become necessary," he told Bernama today.
He said checks were also conducted at Taman Bendahara, where accommodation for Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) students is located, and conditions there remained under control.
He said that his team would continue monitoring high-risk areas to ensure immediate action could be taken should water levels rise.
The public has also been advised to remain vigilant, stay alert to their surroundings and comply with the authorities' instructions if asked to evacuate.

Title: 137 invasive redtail catfish weighing over 1,000kg caught in Pahang
Article:
KUANTAN: A total of 137 invasive redtail catfish weighing more than 1,000kg were caught during the Pahang 1st: Tawan Baung Ekor Merah Fest programme held at seven locations.
The programme was a joint initiative by the Pahang government, the Fisheries Department and the Pahang Youth Council to intensify efforts to control and reduce the redtail catfish population, which could threaten the balance of inland aquatic ecosystems and the survival of local fish species.
Fisheries Department director-general Datuk Adnan Hussain said that addressing the threat posed by invasive fish species such as the redtail catfish required continuous action and cooperation from all parties to ensure the balance of inland aquatic ecosystems was maintained.
"This programme is a proactive approach to reducing the redtail catfish population in Pahang waters. The threat posed by invasive fish species must be addressed continuously to protect local fish species and maintain the balance of aquatic ecosystems," he said in a statement today.
The participation of 1,110 anglers at the seven locations demonstrated that the community had an important role to play in helping the government address the threat posed by invasive fish species, he added.
"This cooperation between the Pahang government, the Fisheries Department and the Pahang Youth Council should continue to strengthen community involvement, particularly among youths and the angling community, in efforts to conserve fisheries resources and protect inland aquatic biodiversity," he said.
He the threat posed by invasive fish species should not be taken lightly, as their presence could disrupt food chains, trigger competition for habitats and threaten the survival of local fish species.
"The Fisheries Department will continue to intensify efforts to monitor and control the populations of invasive fish species, while raising public awareness against releasing non-local fish into public waters.
"Community cooperation is crucial to ensuring that the country's inland aquatic biodiversity and fisheries resources remain protected," he said.
Based on the overall results, Tanjung Gahai in Lipis recorded the highest total catch weight at 193.50kg from 16 fish, followed by Pekan with 191.44 kg (23 fish) and Kuala Krau in Temerloh with 182.38 kg (30 fish).
The state government was reported to have allocated RM450,000 for the programme to control the redtail catfish, which had been identified as a potential threat to the state's local fish population if left unchecked.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the programme was held simultaneously at seven locations statewide, including Pekan, Jerantut and Kuantan, as part of efforts to reduce the population of the invasive fish species. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schumer led Democrats to big Senate win but some now want new leader
Article:
CHUCK Schumer led Senate Democrats through November's midterm elections that gave them a decisive 56-seat majority.
Progressives responded with a collective "thank you, next," arguing he should now make way for a successor.
Critics say Schumer's decades in Washington, his age and his close ties to the party establishment make him ill-suited to lead a caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.
"We write first to thank you," leaders of the populist Working Families Party, which backs like-minded Democratic candidates in elections, said in a Nov 13 letter to Schumer that called for a generational leadership change.
"If you step aside at the height of a victory you helped secure, you would show voters that the Democratic Party heeded their call for change.
"The new majority can begin its work united and focused on fighting for the people who elected them."
The top Democrat in the Senate for the past decade, Schumer, who turns 76 on Monday, has projected confidence that his colleagues will choose to keep him as their leader in a secret vote on Dec 1.
"I will be elected majority leader," Schumer, who is strongly favored to win, told reporters matter-of-factly last week.
But in the first contested Senate Democratic leadership race since 1994, the New York senator faces a challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen, 67.
While only modestly younger than Schumer, the Maryland lawmaker and his progressive allies outside the Capitol have cast him as an agent of change.
Van Hollen has said the 2026 results show voters are demanding the party break with the status quo and adopt a bolder approach that gives new voices, including incoming progressive lawmakers, more influence in the caucus.
The Maryland Democrat has run an increasingly public campaign, though the outcome will be determined in private by 56 Senate Democrats.
At least 16 Democrats have publicly committed to backing Schumer, while only six have said they will vote for Van Hollen.
"I'm in this to win it," Van Hollen said on Thursday.
"That's my goal. I think if we want to move forward on an ambitious agenda like this, we need new leadership. We need to change the culture of the Democratic caucus. People need to have more input. Our new members need to be at the table."
[[nid:1583428]]
Democrats flipped nine Senate seats in November, including in several states President Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024.
Many of the incoming freshmen said during their campaigns that they would oppose Schumer for Democratic leader.
"Do I like Chuck Schumer?" asked Senator-elect Troy Jackson of Maine. "He's been great, but I do think it's time for new ideas."
In an interview last week on CNN's "State of the Union," Van Hollen cited a "hunger for change" among Senate Democrats and said two incoming senators won despite Schumer's efforts to back their primary opponents.
He criticised Schumer for aligning with powerful pro-Israel and cryptocurrency interests in those races.
Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said Van Hollen stands out because he understands how Washington and the Senate work as a past chair of House and Senate Democrats' respective campaign arms, and he's willing to take risks.
"Those two things are what we need right now, and we need to rethink the way we legislate," he said, pointing to Van Hollen's trips to advocate for a wrongly deported migrant and to draw attention to Israel's war in Gaza as examples of his willingness to take risks.
Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia suggested the leadership fight reflected a healthy discussion within the caucus about its future direction. "And there's nothing wrong with that," he told Reuters.
Senate Democratic leader is the only unresolved role among Congress' top four positions.
House Democrats last week nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker in the next Congress, where John Thune will continue to lead Senate Republicans and Representative Jim Jordan will succeed Speaker Mike Johnson as the top House Republican.
Schumer is up for reelection in 2028, and losing the leadership race could make him a more vulnerable target, as ambitious Democrats such as Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez consider running for his seat.
A memo from Ocasio-Cortez's campaign acknowledged she could run for president, Senate or reelection to the House in 2028.
For his part, Schumer has swatted down questions about his future beyond the leadership election.
"I'm focused on 2027 and delivering for the American people," he said on Wednesday.
* The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Poor Selangor DAP convention turnout prompts Loke's warning to absent leaders
Article:
SHAH ALAM: DAP leaders who skipped the party's Selangor convention today risk losing their positions, with secretary-general Anthony Loke warning that those who showed no commitment to the party would not be given a second chance.
He said Selangor DAP chairman Ng Sze Han had been instructed to review and submit a list of members who were absent, particularly leaders such as assemblymen, village heads and local councillors.
"Village heads and councillors who were absent must be blacklisted and not have their contracts renewed.
"If any assemblyman is absent today, give me their names. This is a basic responsibility. If they cannot even show the most basic commitment, don't talk about the struggle, wanting to be a candidate," he said in his speech at the Selangor DAP Convention at SITC, Section 14.
Loke said he had to take firm action in the party's interest, even if it might not sit well with some quarters.
He said those who failed to show dedication to the party should not be surprised if it withdrew its support for them in the next election.
"If you want to use your branches or delegates to bring me down, go ahead. But I will ensure that those who have no commitment will have no place," he said.
"Today, I can see that the fighting spirit is not strong enough. Attendance has not been encouraging because there is no party election.
"When there is a party election, I don't even need to say anything. The hall will be full. Our branches were not established for party elections. We were established to carry the torch of the party's struggle.
"Whether there is a party election or not, good attendance at conventions is compulsory. This is a party in government. We are part of the state government," he said.
Loke also said DAP was in crisis mode, claiming that certain quarters wanted to bring down the party and the government.
"We are in crisis mode and need to act immediately.
"Others want to bring down our party and our government. We must be serious in our struggle and regain the spirit to defend and fight for the party, just as we did in 2008," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Senate deputy president Halim Abd Samad dies at 86
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former deputy president of the Senate, Datuk Seri Abdul Halim Abd Samad, died today at the age of 86 due to a lung infection.
His youngest brother, Zulkhairi Abd Samad said his brother breathed his last at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) around 4.20pm today.
The deceased had been suffering from lung disease for several years before experiencing heart valve damage and was frequently being admitted to the hospital.
"Yesterday, the deceased suddenly lost consciousness and the doctor said that it was likely due to a bacterial infection in the lungs," Zulkhairi said when contacted by Bernama.
He said Halim's remains are currently at his residence at Jalan Jelatek, Kampung Datuk Keramat and are expected to buried in Gombak tomorrow morning.
Halim, who hailed from Kuantan, Pahang, leaves behind his wife, Iasah Ibrahim, and three children.
He was appointed as a Senator on Nov 3, 2014, and served as the deputy president of the Dewan Negara from April 18, 2016, to Nov 2, 2020.
He once served as a school teacher, press secretary, and senior private secretary to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, and was the first chief of Federal Territory Umno Youth.
He was also KUB Malaysia Bhd Group chairman and was involved in community welfare associations.
Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid his respects to Halim at the family's residence.
"Losing a loved one is certainly not something easy to go through. May the entire family be granted strength and resilience in facing this moment filled with sorrow," said Zahid, who is also Umno president, in a Facebook post.
He also invited the public to pray that Allah SWT forgives all Halim's sins, accepts his good deeds, and places his soul among the faithful and righteous. — BERNAMA

Title: Kedah Immigration arrests 52 foreigners in construction site raid
Article:
ALOR STAR: A total of 52 foreigners were arrested by the Kedah Immigration Department during an operation at a construction site this morning.
In a statement, the department said those detained comprised 38 Bangladeshi men, 13 Indonesians (10 men and three women) and a Myanmar man, aged between 19 and 55.
A total of 64 people were screened, including eight Malaysians.
They were detained under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the Immigration Regulations 1963, with most found to be without valid travel documents or passes.
The department also found that some foreign workers were using employment passes registered under companies other than their actual employers.
A witness summons was issued to assist further investigations.
Immigration deputy director-general (Operations) Loqman Effendi Ramli was also present.
Kedah Immigration reminded employers to ensure foreign workers held valid Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) and worked only for approved employers and in authorised sectors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fake accounts posing as second finance minister, Treasury sec-gen surface online
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public is advised to be vigilant and not to be deceived by fake social media accounts that use the names and photographs of Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan and secretary-general of the Treasury Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican.
The Finance Ministry (MoF), in two separate Facebook posts today, stated that these accounts could potentially mislead the public for instance, through posts and messages urging individuals to contact specific phone numbers to apply for financial assistance.
"The public is advised not to easily trust social media accounts that use the names or photographs of government leaders without verification," the statement read.
MoF urged the public not to share personal information, banking details, or one-time passwords (OTP) with unknown parties, and to refrain from making any payments or following suspicious instructions received through such accounts.
The public is encouraged to obtain authentic information via the ministry's official communication channels at www.mof.gov.my. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police investigate viral claims of extortion, bribery at Penang roadblock
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Police are investigating a viral social media post alleging that traffic policemen had committed extortion and accepted bribes during a roadblock.
Northeast police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said they detected the post today after it drew widespread public attention.
He confirmed that a police report had been lodged.
"Police are investigating the incident depicted in the viral post involving the traffic personnel under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998," he said in a statement.
Rozak said the investigation would also cover compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and disciplinary aspects involving the personnel concerned.

Title: Fadhlina: Character building must begin at preschool level
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Values education and character building should begin at preschool age to nurture respect and empathy in children.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said quality education was not merely about teaching children to read, write and count, but also about shaping them into individuals with good values and strong character.
"This effort certainly requires the support of parents, teachers and the community at large. What is taught in school must also be nurtured at home, as children learn not only from what we tell them but also from what they observe in their daily lives," she said in a Facebook post today.
Fadhlina also expressed her appreciation for the concern and views expressed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over increasingly worrying social issues involving the young generation.
"The concern by His Royal Highness serves as a reminder that efforts to shape a child's character cannot wait until they reach their teenage years," she said.
On Nov 18, Tuanku Muhriz voiced concern over the rise in social problems among youths, prompting the introduction of the Modul Aulad Sejahtera (Child Well-being Module), an early intervention initiative aimed at shaping character, instilling noble values and strengthening children's identity from the preschool level.
His Royal Highness said the module was developed in response to worrying social trends, including drug abuse, illegal street racing and other negative behaviours that threaten the future of the young generation.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said 8,365 preschool pupils under the Education Ministry (MOE) in Negri Sembilan would benefit from the Modul Aulad Sejahtera, which emphasises the development of good conduct (adab), noble values, emotional well-being and social skills.
She expressed hope that the initiative, introduced in Negri Sembilan, could serve as a model for nurturing a knowledgeable generation with strong cultural values.

Title: Rough waters no reason to sink the ship, Abang Johari tells GPS members
Article:
KUCHING:KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) component parties must remain united and not allow differences of opinion to sink the coalition's ship as it navigates the rough waters ahead of the 13th Sarawak state election, says its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The Sarawak Premier said differences of opinion were inevitable during an election, but the coalition's component parties must ensure that such differences did not derail their shared goals.
He said the entire election machinery must work together to keep the GPS vessel on course, guided by a spirit of camaraderie.
"During an election, all sorts of things happen. Which sea is without rough waters? There are bound to be some waves, but do not sink the ship. Let the ship, with its captain and crew, sail toward a glorious destination.
"The engines must be in good working order, and the technicians tending to them must be able to read the compass. If the compass isn't set correctly, you'll end up somewhere else.
"You need people who know how to read the 'GPS compass'. We have a compass, a 'GPS' compass crafted by Sarawakians, so let us move forward," he said during the launch of the GPS election machinery at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK).
Abang Johari, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) president, said the spirit of camaraderie, rooted in firm mutual trust, must be upheld to ensure political stability and the state's development.
Earlier, Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) president Datuk Seri
Tiong King Sing
said his party intended to defend all eight state seats it currently held in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Tiong expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party's election machinery, coupled with the commitment of its leadership and members, would ensure that all eight seats remained with PDP under the GPS coalition.
GPS comprises PBB, Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.
The
Election Commission
has set Nov 28 as nomination day, Dec 8 for early voting and Dec 12 as polling day.

Title: Sarawak polls: PDP to defend eight seats under GPS banner
Article:
KUCHING: The Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) aims to defend all eight state legislative assembly seats currently held by the party in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Party president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing expressed confidence that the preparedness of the party machinery, combined with the commitment of the entire PDP leadership and its members, would ensure that all eight seats remain under the party's fold within the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) coalition.
"As the party president, I wish to emphasise that we intend to retain all eight seats currently held by the PDP. I have full confidence in the wisdom and leadership of Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to continue safeguarding harmony within GPS," he said.
He made these remarks while speaking at the launch of the Gabungan Parti Sarawak election machinery for the 13th Sarawak state election.
Meanwhile, Tiong clarified that he has not yet submitted the PDP's list of candidates, despite claims circulating that the list had already been handed over to the GPS leadership.
He said his party's list of candidates would be submitted to Abang Johari who also serves as the chairman of GPS no later than this coming Monday and will take into account the views of the coalition's leadership regarding candidate selection criteria, including factors such as age.
Five of the eight seats currently held by PDP, namely, Tasik Biru, Meluan, Krian, Marudi, and Dudong were won by the party during the 12th Sarawak state election while the remaining seats of Bawang Assan, Engkilili, and Ba'kelalan were acquired following the dissolution of Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) and the subsequent absorption of its members into the PDP as a bloc.
Abang Johari was reported as saying that the full list of the coalition's 82 candidates for the Sarawak state election will be announced on Nov 25.
The Election Commission (EC) has set the polling day for the 13th Sarawak state election for Dec 12, with nomination day scheduled for November 28 and early voting for Dec 8.

Title: GST should start at 3pct to ease cost of living, says consumer group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The next government should consider reintroducing the Goods and Services Tax (GST) at an initial rate of three per cent to ease the cost of living, says the Kedah Consumers Association (CAKE).
Its president, Mohamad Yusrizal Yusoff, said the proposed rate would be more reasonable than the previous six per cent, given that prices of essential goods were already high compared with income levels.
He said the rising cost of living had put pressure on consumers and businesses, as declining purchasing power led to slower sales.
"If the GST can help ease the burden on the people, it should be introduced at a lower rate of three per cent initially.
"At the same time, we hope full exemptions will be granted for essential goods and purchases made by those in the bottom 40 per cent income group (B40) to ease their financial burden," he said.
He was commenting on a statement by Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who pledged to reintroduce the GST if the coalition returned to power after the 16th general election (GE16).
Zahid, who is also the deputy prime minister,
described the GST
as a fairer and more targeted taxation system than the Sales and Service Tax (SST) currently in place.
He said more than 170 countries had implemented the GST and that Malaysia should reinstate it to avoid falling behind other nations.
On the differences between the GST and SST, Mohamad Yusrizal said the current SST system resulted in overlapping or multiple layers of taxation along the supply chain.
He said the eight per cent tax imposed at different stages, from manufacturers to wholesalers and retailers, contributed to a gradual increase in the final prices of goods.
"In contrast, the GST allows manufacturers and wholesalers to claim input tax credits, making the calculation process more transparent and fair.
"However, confusion arose previously due to a lack of clear explanations to consumers.
"The detailed breakdown of taxes on purchase receipts also made people feel more burdened compared with the SST, where taxes are incorporated into selling prices," he said.
Meanwhile, Yusrizal said the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry should take more proactive measures to prevent unjustified price increases.
He said the ministry already had the necessary legal provisions under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 to curb profiteering and protect consumer rights.
"The ministry should fully utilise the existing legislation to prevent profiteering and safeguard consumers," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shoes tax break: Cultivating a culture of well-being
Article:
LETTER:
At first glance, the act of including sports shoes in the tax relief list under Budget 2027 might seem like a rather small, even amusing, announcement.
We should look beyond the shoes themselves and consider what this measure represents. Malaysia is facing a growing public health challenge.
The Ministry of Health's National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2024: Nutrition found that 30.5 per cent of Malaysian adults were overweight, 23.1 per cent were obese and more than half, or 52.1 per cent, also had abdominal obesity.
Being overweight can increase the risk of health problems such as diabetes and heart disease, which may require long-term treatment and add to the demands on our healthcare system.
These findings highlight the scale of the challenge facing the country, with implications for families, workplaces, and public resources.
Earlier findings from NHMS 2023 showed that 29.9 per cent of adults were physically inactive, underlining the importance of creating more opportunities for Malaysians to lead active lives.
Obesity is rarely the result of one decision or one bad habit.
It develops through a combination of factors, including diet, physical activity, working patterns, the environment, and access to opportunities for healthier living.
For Malaysians balancing work, family commitments and the rising cost of living, finding time for exercise can easily take a back seat.
This is where the seemingly ordinary pair of sports shoes becomes relevant.
For someone who already runs regularly, the tax relief may simply be a welcome saving on a purchase they would have made anyway.
But for someone who has been thinking about taking up walking or starting a simple exercise routine, it could provide a small push in the right direction.
It may not be the deciding factor, but it can help make the first step feel a little more achievable.
For beginners, especially those who are overweight or have not exercised for years, comfort and appropriate support may influence whether they continue an activity or abandon it after a few uncomfortable attempts.
Of course, we should be clear about what the Budget 2027 measure offers. The inclusion of sports shoes under the existing sports-related tax relief does not mean every Malaysian will receive free shoes or a cash payment.
Under Budget 2027, eligible taxpayers can claim tax relief on sports shoes, subject to a limit of RM300 within the existing overall sports-related tax relief limit of RM1,000.
The challenge is to ensure that the tax relief forms part of a broader effort rather than remaining a standalone measure.
Encouraging people to buy sports shoes is only useful if it leads them to be physically active.
More parks and recreational spaces are needed, while walking paths should be properly maintained and extended to more urban areas.
These improvements would make walking more accessible and encourage people to choose it over driving whenever practical.
Workplaces can also play a role by introducing wellness programmes, organising group walks or exercise sessions, and allowing employees reasonable breaks to move throughout the working day.
We must also move away from the idea that exercise is reserved for people who are already fit.
A healthier lifestyle does not have to begin with a marathon, an expensive gym membership, or a demanding workout programme.
It can begin with a ten-minute walk after dinner, taking the stairs when practical, or walking to a nearby shop instead of driving.
These may appear insignificant individually, but they can help establish habits that become part of everyday life.
The sports shoe tax relief is therefore best understood as a modest incentive, not a cure.
Its success should not be measured by how many pairs of shoes Malaysians purchase, but by whether it contributes to a wider culture that values movement, prevention, and personal well-being.
A government that recognises the importance of exercise in its fiscal policies is acknowledging that health deserves attention beyond hospitals and clinics.
NUR FARAH IDAYU SAADON
Training consultant
National Institute of Public Administration (INTAN)

Title: DOSM to conduct household income, expenditure and basic amenities survey next year
Article:
IPOH: The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) will conduct the 6th Household Income, Expenditure and Basic Amenities Survey (HIES/BA) 2027 from Jan 1 to Dec 31 next year.
In a statement, DOSM said the survey aims to collect data on household income, expenditure, and basic amenities to produce official statistics regarding expenditure patterns, poverty rates, cost of living, and income inequality.
"The statistics produced serve as a basis for planning and policy formulation by stakeholders toward improving the well-being of the people," according to the statement.
In the same statement, DOSM said it provides a data catalog and visualisations to facilitate users in analysing various data through OpenDOSM NextGen, which can be accessed via the portal https://open.dosm.gov.my.
Meanwhile, DOSM implemented six community development projects worth RM500,000 in Kampung Menderang, Sungkai, through the Kampung Angkat Madani 2026 Programme.
The initiative is a strategic collaboration between the government and the local community to empower rural development inclusively and sustainably, in line with the Malaysia Madani aspirations.
"All completed projects include the construction of basic village facilities and infrastructure, the installation of signboards, and the installation of solar lights around the area.
"In addition, the development initiative also includes upgrading works for mosque, surau, and sports court facilities," the statement said.

Title: Flood situation improves in Selangor, Perak as evacuee numbers drop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Flood situations in Selangor and Perak continued to improve, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres declining to 2,151 people from 615 families this afternoon, compared with 2,315 people from 689 families this morning.
In
SELANGOR
, the number dropped to 1,727 people from 484 families, compared with 1,884 people from 532 families recorded this morning.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, the evacuees were housed at several relief centres, including SK Dato' Maharaja Lela (397), SK Parit Mahang (360), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (180), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (135), SRA Batu 8 Ijok (120) and SK Rantau Panjang (four).
Other centres were SK Sultan Abdul Aziz (223 evacuees), SK Jaya Setia (73), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (65), Seri Harmoni Community Hall (36), SK Batu Arang (25), Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (16) and SRA Pasangan (93).
In
PERAK
, the number of evacuees at five relief centres in four districts also dropped to 424 people from 131 families this afternoon, compared with 479 people from 157 families this morning.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said the SK Tanjung Belanja relief centre in Perak Tengah was closed at 2 pm after all 53 evacuees from 25 families were allowed to return home after floodwaters receded.
Meanwhile, SRA Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung recorded 129 evacuees from 38 families, while the Teluk Intan Municipal Council Rest House Hall in Hilir Perak continued to house 97 people from 31 families.
In Kerian, the number of evacuees remained unchanged at 176 people from 55 families, including 12 landslide victims from three families, who were sheltering at SK Bukit Merah and SK Parit Haji Aman.
The number of flood evacuees in Larut, Matang and Selama also remained unchanged at 10 people from four families, housed at SK Batu Hampar.

Title: [UPDATED] Search for Indonesia factory fire missing to resume Monday, police remove 24 body bags
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesian police removed 24 body bags from a factory destroyed by fire in Java on Sunday as firefighters battled remaining hotspots a day after the blaze tore through the building and a search for dozens of missing workers was suspended overnight.
The fire broke out on Saturday evening at the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Cikande, in the Serang regency. The factory is part of Indonesia's United Family Food company, founded in 1981, according to its website.
Metro TV footage showed distraught family members weeping outside the factory as they waited for news of relatives feared to have been caught in the blaze.
Search operations are scheduled to resume on Monday morning, Hendra Kurniawan, the police chief of Indonesia's Banten province, told Metro TV.
Steven Erwin Wijaya, the CEO of the factory, said at a press conference that around 300 people were present for Saturday's shift.
In a later statement, the factory said that 24 of the 65 workers involved had returned home, 4 were receiving medical treatment, 29 remained missing and the whereabouts of another 8 had yet to be confirmed.
At the same press conference, Wahyu Hidayati, a police disaster victim identification official, said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable via visual inspection, prompting efforts to collect DNA samples from relatives and the personal belongings of the missing workers, a process that could take two to three weeks.
The number of dead was not immediately clear, with police saying that one body bag could contain parts of more than one person.
Authorities said the cause of the fire was being investigated. Parts of the building remained at risk of collapse, an official added.
United Family Food produces consumer goods across Indonesia, employs about 5,000 people and operates from its national headquarters and four international offices, serving a market of more than 250 million consumers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Death toll from spurious liquor in India's Manipur rises to 16
Article:
NEW DELHI: The death toll from spurious liquor consumption in India's northeastern state of Manipur has risen to 16, while around 600 people are undergoing treatment in different hospitals, officials said Saturday, reported Xinhua.
The incident took place in the Chakpikarong area of Chandel district, about 75 km south of Imphal, the capital city of Manipur.
"The death toll in the spurious liquor incident has risen to 16," a local government official said.
According to the state-run broadcaster All India Radio (AIR), around 600 people have been admitted to various government and private hospitals.
A senior local government official in Manipur, Hungyo Worshang, told the media that teams from the district administration, police, excise and health departments have visited the affected areas and hospitals to assess the situation and provide necessary assistance.
Police have arrested six people in connection with the incident.
The local government of Manipur has constituted a high-level inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify possible lapses and recommend necessary action.
Officials said the committee has been asked to submit its report within one month.
"Samples of the suspected liquor have been sent for forensic examination to identify the presence of toxic substances," the official said.
Manipur health department has issued a public health advisory in view of the suspected spurious liquor-related deaths and illnesses.
The health department has directed all government and private healthcare facilities to remain alert and ensure prompt treatment, referral and reporting of suspected cases.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lahore tops the list of most polluted cities in the world
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Hazardous smog turned Pakistan's second-largest city into the most polluted metropolis on the planet on Sunday, leaving authorities helpless to curb pollution, reported German news agency dpa.
The air quality in Lahore had a pollutant concentration reading of 289, making it the most-polluted city in the world, according to IQAir, a global environmental think tank.
The eastern city bordering India consistently ranked as the world's most polluted major city in the past few weeks since thick and hazardous smog engulfed parts of the central Punjab province.
Motorways connecting major cities were closed for traffic due to poor visibility at various points by authorities in addition to anti-smog measures that include fines on smoke-emitting vehicles.
Pakistani authorities blame industrial emissions, smoke from brick kilns and vehicles, the burning of crop residue and general waste for being behind the air pollution and smog in Lahore.
Pakistan is responsible for less than one per cent of global carbon emissions but is among the top 10 most climate-vulnerable nations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chow rejects Guan Eng's 'unethical' Penang-Perak water deal claims
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has rebuked Bagan member of parliament Lim Guan Eng for repeatedly alleging unethical conduct in the Perak-Penang bulk water deal.
Chow, who chairs PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAHB) and Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP), said it was regrettable that Lim continued to repeat the allegations despite repeated explanations about the Bulk Water Supply Agreement (BWSA).
In a statement, Chow questioned why securing 40 years of water supply for residents, industries, investors and future generations could be considered unethical.
He said the agreement had received approval from all PBAPP board members and secured 98 per cent shareholder support at PBAHB's extraordinary general meeting (EGM) on Nov 12.
Addressing concerns over the board's decision, Chow said the views and professionalism of five PBAHB independent directors had been recorded and respected during the meeting, which passed the agreement by a majority vote of seven to five.
"Their objections were solely focused on specific payment terms, which have already been addressed through clauses in the agreement," he said.
Lim had recently accused Chow of acting
unethically
by dismissing concerns over the state's RM8.4 billion water deal with Perak.
He said Chow had disrespected the financial judgement and professionalism of five independent directors of PBAHB who objected to the agreement's terms.
Chow also dismissed Lim's allegation that PBAPP would be forced to pay RM210 million annually for 40 years without receiving a single drop of water, describing the portrayal as misleading and unethical.
He said PBAPP was not required to make any payment to Perak before water supply implementation began, and any disbursement remained subject to approval by the National Water Services Commission.
Under the arrangement, Penang would gain access to substantial water infrastructure capacity without bearing the full construction costs and early-stage development risks.
Chow added that PBAPP held contractual rights to take action, including invoking termination mechanisms, if unrectified breaches occurred.
"This means Penang is not locked into paying until 2072 as claimed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi allocates RM50k for mass communication students
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has announced a RM50,000 contribution to a coalition of mass communication student clubs to encourage student development programmes.
The contribution is aimed at strengthening the coalition and helping students face future challenges, particularly the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on journalism and mass communication, he said.
Fahmi also proposed expanding the coalition to all public universities before bringing private universities offering mass communication courses on board.
"I welcome the formation of a coalition of student clubs from mass communication courses or faculties. I understand that five universities are represented today.
"To encourage them to plan programmes in the future, I am announcing a contribution of RM50,000 to the coalition.
"I have also asked for it to be expanded to all public universities and subsequently to private universities with mass communication faculties or courses," he said.
He was speaking after officiating the Communication and Media Student National Convention, organised by Universiti Teknologi MARA's Faculty of Communication and Media Studies, here today.
Also present was UiTM Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Academic and International) Professor Dr Yamin Yasin, who is performing the functions of the vice-chancellor.
Fahmi said students had frequently raised concerns about their career prospects, particularly the impact of AI on journalism, during his engagements at universities.
He said he wanted to increase engagement with students to hear their concerns and explain the government's efforts to protect journalists' jobs and the future of journalism and mass communication in the age of AI.
"I see the need for more engagement with university students, not only to listen to their concerns but also to explain the government's efforts, particularly to protect journalists' jobs and the future of journalism and mass communication with the presence of AI," he said.
Fahmi also acknowledged the contributions of strategic partners, including Bank Muamalat and Tenaga Nasional Berhad, to student development programmes.
He hoped partnerships, particularly with government-linked companies and corporate bodies, would help expand such programmes and bring them closer to university students.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No shortcuts, no instant paste: How Banglo289 keeps traditional Malay cuisine authentic at mid-market prices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 —  In an increasingly competitive food and beverage industry, the use of instant ingredients and commercial pastes has become a common choice among food operators, particularly to save preparation time and reduce costs.
However, Banglo289, a restaurant serving traditional Malay cuisine from various states, has chosen to go against the grain by using fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods to preserve the authenticity of its dishes.
The restaurant also offers a unique dining concept, combining an upscale and comfortable setting with prices aimed at the mid-market segment.
“The idea behind setting up this restaurant actually stemmed from our observation of a gap in the market for traditional food, particularly Malay cuisine, served in a comfortable setting at reasonable prices.
“Usually, if customers want to enjoy this type of food at affordable prices, roadside stalls are their best option, but the surroundings may not be very comfortable. If they prefer a more comfortable setting, there are exclusive restaurants, but they have to pay premium prices,” its Chief Executive Officer Shareen Farzida Sukri told Bernama.
Making heritage cuisine accessible
Banglo289 seeks to bridge that gap by offering an exclusive dining environment and a wide selection of dishes, allowing customers to choose their preferred food and portions according to their tastes and budgets.
The Kelantan-born entrepreneur from Kuala Krai said the average spending of between RM30 and RM50 per person per visit recorded by the restaurant did not refer to the fixed price of any particular dish, but rather the total amount customers typically spent during each visit.
“This includes a combination of rice, side dishes, vegetables, porridge, desserts, fruits and traditional cakes, all reflected in a single bill,” she explained.
The menu also varies according to dining hours, with different selections available for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Recounting the restaurant’s establishment in 2022, Shareen Farzida said that, as its name suggests, the premises occupy a century-old bungalow located along Jalan Raja Chulan here.
Within four years of operation, the restaurant brand has expanded to four outlets at different locations across the Klang Valley, with plans to open more branches in other states nationwide.
Balancing costs and business sustainability
The expansion has also brought greater responsibilities, particularly in ensuring that the concept and quality of food remain consistent across all outlets, a task Shareen Farzida acknowledged posed challenges, especially in terms of costs.
Using fresh ingredients, including spices, requires employees to prepare basic ingredients themselves, such as fresh chillies, onions and turmeric.
“The cost of fresh coconut milk alone reaches RM50,000 a month for all our outlets. We adopt this approach to ensure the authenticity of our food.
“Previous generations, such as our mothers and grandmothers, rarely or never used instant ingredients, possibly because of preservatives and chemicals that could affect the original taste of the dishes,” she said.
To demonstrate its commitment to preparing basic ingredients from scratch without relying on instant pastes, the restaurant has incorporated open-kitchen concepts near the serving counters at almost all its outlets, allowing customers to observe the cooking process firsthand.
Minimising food wastage
Shareen Farzida said rising raw material prices were managed through careful operational planning to ensure that the restaurant did not compromise on food quality.
“Among the cost-saving measures we have introduced are those that do not affect the taste of our food, such as opting for simpler decorations and food presentation that are not overly elaborate but remain neat and visually appealing.
“We also focus on improving workforce management by arranging staff shifts and allocating duties according to peak and off-peak hours, ensuring productivity remains high without placing an excessive burden on salary costs,” she explained.
The restaurant also prioritises efficient raw material management, with each outlet having its own purchasing team to source fresh ingredients according to the respective kitchen’s requirements.
“Raw ingredients must be used on the same day and cannot be kept for use on another day.
“We have adopted this approach to minimise wastage and keep our overhead costs under control. This is why dishes are prepared in stages and in small batches of only about 10 to 15 servings at a time, with no leftover dishes kept for the following day.
“If a particular dish is in high demand, additional portions can be prepared as long as operating hours and the availability of raw ingredients permit,” she said.
She added that the restaurant sometimes had to explain its concept to customers, particularly its practice of preparing food in controlled quantities to maintain quality and prevent wastage.
Nevertheless, she said certain best-selling dishes, such as smoked beef cooked in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies (daging salai masak lemak cili api), were always made available to customers.
Traditional cooking
To preserve the authenticity of its traditional dishes, Banglo289 also takes the initiative to learn heritage cooking techniques directly from their original sources.
Banglo289 Business Development Director Datuk Mohd Hafidz Safari Ramli said research teams, usually comprising between six and 12 chefs, travelled to selected states, including Kelantan, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Johor, to meet veteran cooks and local communities who still possessed knowledge of traditional food preparation.
“This research is an ongoing learning process. Each visit is not merely about obtaining a list of ingredients, but also understanding the entire process, from selecting raw materials and determining measurements to the sequence of cooking steps and the time required to produce an authentic dish,” he said.
He added that the teams would revisit the original sources if their attempts to recreate a dish did not meet the desired characteristics, whether in terms of taste, colour or texture.
Every recipe and cooking method learnt is documented as a reference for the chefs, helping to ensure consistent food quality even when dishes are prepared by different individuals.
Citing Kelantan’s nasi dagang as an example, he said the team not only learnt its preparation methods directly from local sources in the state but also sourced ingredients, including spices, from there.
For patin fish cooked in fermented durian paste gravy (patin masak tempoyak), the research team travelled to Temerloh, Pahang, to understand the balance of sourness and the distinctive consistency of the gravy.
Meanwhile, the preparation of smoked beef in coconut milk with bird’s eye chillies involves manually smoking the meat over rambutan wood and coconut shells for approximately eight hours.
“All these are part of the preparation process that cannot simply be bypassed. If we want to preserve our cultural heritage through food, we must do it properly and uphold the true meaning of the word ‘heritage’,” he said.
Reviving endangered heritage dishes
Apart from preserving the authenticity of traditional dishes that remain familiar to the public, Banglo289 is also committed to reviving heritage cuisine that is becoming increasingly difficult to find, particularly dishes that are no longer widely prepared by restaurant operators or younger generations.
Shareen Farzida said the initiative, known as ‘Endangered Recipes’, stemmed from her team’s observations of the diversity of traditional food in several locations, including dishes that were known or still prepared by only a handful of food operators and elderly cooks.
Among the dishes identified for preservation are lemang periuk kera, kulat sisir masak lemak, lawar terung and bubur anak lebah, each with its own distinctive ingredients and preparation techniques.
Citing bubur anak lebah as an example, she explained that the traditional sweet delicacy, made from a rice flour-based batter, requires considerable manual skill and a special mould to shape tiny pieces resembling baby bees before they are cooked until chewy and served with sweet coconut milk gravy.
Preparing such unique dishes requires patience and direct guidance, as the techniques cannot necessarily be mastered through written recipes alone, she said.
She added that the team’s visits to several states had also uncovered dishes that were prepared only during Ramadan or certain festive seasons, limiting opportunities for younger generations to discover and learn how to make them.
This has raised concerns that the knowledge and skills involved could disappear if those who still possess them pass away before having the opportunity to pass them on.
“That is why we plan to collaborate with Yayasan Hasanah, an impact-driven foundation under Khazanah Nasional Berhad that actively supports the preservation of local arts, heritage and culture, to fund the production of a special documentary on this ongoing project.
“Heritage cuisine is not merely a cultural treasure to be printed on a menu. It is a body of knowledge and a cultural identity that must continue to be cooked, savoured, documented and passed down properly, without shortcuts,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Thailand only a transit route for drug syndicates targeting Malaysia, says Kelantan police chief after 700kg meth bust
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 21 — Malaysia-Thailand cross-border security cooperation has continued to strengthen, with authorities in the neighbouring country successfully preventing more than 700 kilogrammes of methamphetamine from entering Malaysia.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the success demonstrated the Thai authorities’ commitment to combating drug smuggling activities that use the country as a transit route before the drugs are brought into Malaysia.
He said Thailand was not the main destination for the drug smuggling activities but served primarily as a transit route for syndicates involved in cross-border crime.
Mohd Yusoff said Kelantan police had previously held meetings with the Thai authorities to strengthen security cooperation, particularly in combating drug smuggling and criminal activities along the border of the two countries.
“The Thai authorities have taken steps to tighten security by setting up checkpoints to prevent cross-border criminal activities, including the entry of drugs into Malaysia.
“What we have implemented on our side has also been adopted by Thailand, and they have now stepped up their security measures. We are grateful for the cooperation and commitment shown,” he told reporters after an engagement programme with young bikers at the Kelantan police contingent headquarters here today.
Mohd Yusoff said close cooperation between the two countries was important to ensure that border routes were not exploited by syndicates to carry out drug smuggling activities.
He said enhanced joint security measures could also help curb the movement of syndicates using cross-border routes to smuggle illicit substances into the country. — Bernama

Title: Four teenagers under 15 arrested after ramming police car during chase on North-South Expressway
Article:
IPOH, Nov 21 — Police detained four underage teenagers (under 15 years old) for allegedly obstructing public servants from performing their duties at Kilometre 286.5 of the North-South Expressway heading north, near Simpang Pulai, yesterday.
Tapah district deputy police chief DSP Mohd Fadzil Ismail said a team of officers on patrol duty received information at 4.20 pm yesterday from the Tapah district police headquarters (IPD) control centre to assist officers from the Ringlet police station in tracking down a Toyota Cherry multi-purpose vehicle occupied by several individuals suspected of being involved in a kidnapping case.
He said that following the information, police officers moved to the Batu 3 area, Jalan Pahang, near Tapah, to conduct a surveillance and the vehicle involved was successfully detected at about 5.30 pm.
“The police instructed the driver of the vehicle to stop for inspection, but the driver failed to comply with the order and instead sped off, nearly hitting the on-duty police officer.
“The police officers then gave chase to the vehicle all the way to the Tapah toll plaza area. In an effort to intercept the suspect’s vehicle, the police vehicle’s bumper was hit by the suspect’s vehicle,” he said in a statement today.
Mohd Fadzil said another police vehicle from the Ipoh district police headquarters joined in the chase before the suspect’s vehicle was successfully intercepted at Simpang Pulai.
He said all four suspects were arrested, and the vehicle they used was seized.
According to him, the initial investigation found that all those detained were teenagers and the results of the urine screening tests showed that they were all drug-free and had no previous records.
“The three teenage boys who were detained have been remanded for four days starting today, while a teenage girl was granted police bail as she is involved in an ongoing investigation in Jitra, Kedah,” he also said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code as well as Section 279 and Section 353 of the same code. — Bernama

Title: Don’t push your child into a boarding school if they’re not ready, Fadhlina tells parents as Education Ministry weighs more wardens and counsellors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 21 — The Ministry of Education is looking into the need to increase the number of assistant wardens and guidance and counselling teachers to ensure students receive optimal attention and support while staying in hostels.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the aspiration of parents to see their children gain admission to fully residential schools should be balanced with the children’s own abilities and emotional readiness.
